judgments.basis: ASC 860-10-40-5(a)-(c) by analogy (isolation, transferee's right to pledge or exchange, no effective control); ASC 610-20 derecognition of nonfinancial assets considered; AICPA Digital Assets Practice Aid crypto lending Q&A; clause 5 grants unrestricted use.
judgments.proposedConclusion: Yes. Applying ASC 860-10-40-5 by analogy, as the AICPA Digital Assets Practice Aid and the SEC staff view do for crypto intangibles: the borrower may sell, lend or re-pledge the ETH without restriction, DemoCo has no right to specific units back, and the ETH is beyond DemoCo's reach. Derecognize the ETH; recognize a crypto asset loan receivable for 100 ETH plus the accrued fee, measured at the fair value of the ETH to be returned at each reporting date with changes in income, and assess it for credit losses under ASC 326.
judgments.question: Did DemoCo surrender control of the 100 ETH such that the ETH (an ASC 350-60 intangible, not a financial asset) is derecognized and a crypto asset loan receivable recognized?

judgments.basis: ASC 326-20-35-6 (collateral maintenance provisions) versus 35-5 (collateral-dependent assets of borrowers in financial difficulty); clause 4 of the agreement; collateral statement; margin-call history.
judgments.proposedConclusion: The agreement requires the borrower to continually adjust USDC collateral to at least 150% of the loan value, marked daily, and the borrower has met every call; the ASC 326-20-35-6 collateral maintenance practical expedient applies and expected credit losses are measured on the unsecured portion — the carrying amount of 250,000 USD less collateral fair value of 400,000 USD, floored at zero — which is zero at 2026-06-30. The 150% margin shortfall is a separate margin-call measure and is not the allowance. The collateral-dependent measurement in 35-5 is not available: the borrower is not in financial difficulty.
